measurement.encoding: explicit Tseitin multipliers/adders, integer f(x1,x2)=q*p, coefficients of S3(.,.,xR) reduced mod p
measurement.note: p=2^24 cells and k>=9 not reached within budget; planted SAT already times out at k=8

reason: Measured c~1.9 (UNSAT) and ~1.6 (SAT) on k=4..7, p~2^20: conflicts grow ~3.5-4.3x per extra bit of k, worse than the 2^k enumerate-x1-and-solve-quadratic baseline, matching the factoring-by-SAT literature (no subexponential carry propagation through multiplier circuits). Structural reason: at k=log p/3 expected solutions are 2^{2k}/p=2^{-k}, so the oracle is overwhelmingly an UNSAT certifier; resolution must refute a degree-4 modular constraint whose reduction mod p destroys carry locality (q has ~3k+ bits of slack), and known resolution/CDCL behaviour on such multiplier-equality instances is exponential with exponent >=1 in the free-bit count. The nongenericity argument is formally valid (it does use the bit representation, so CGK does not apply), but non-genericity alone buys nothing: the measured c is far above the c<1 (and c<1/2 for rho-beating) gate. Scope: kills plain CDCL/XOR resolution solvers on this encoding; does not cover algebraic proof systems (Groebner/polynomial calculus, cutting planes) or lattice-assisted encodings.
fix: none at this scale; a surviving variant would need a non-resolution proof system and must show c<1 itself
collisions: generic oracle bound (not applicable, but dominated)
